title: A plan exists to run the autopilot in a Docker container instead of a separate OS user
goal: kb/_self/autopilot-container.md is a plan, no code yet, that answers: why a container replaces the separate OS user (what each isolates and what it does not, honest limits); the image (base, python3, git, claude CLI, glab, no host tools), built from a pinned Dockerfile kept in the repo; what is mounted (a fresh clone of the integration project only, never the operator's home, SSH agent or main checkout) and what is read-only; credentials (the runner deploy key and token of ST-xiyvkjro passed as secrets at start, never baked in, never printed; the Claude auth path and how the Bedrock token stays stripped); network (allowed hosts only: the git remote, the model API; GitHub denied); resource limits (memory, CPU, pids) sized for the load problems seen; how the tick and runner map onto container start, status, stop and reset, and how backlog.py procs and land cleanup behave inside it; how worktree removal by land works with the container as the only writer; macOS specifics (Docker Desktop or Colima, file-event cost on bind mounts: the fseventsd growth seen on this host); a staged rollout that reuses the test plan stages of kb/_self/autopilot-test.md; and the operator-only gates (credentials, push, agents-rule) as gates with options and a recommendation. Cites code and docs lines, placeholders only, mapped in kb/_self/map.csv.
